product_offering.core_offering: Overjet sells an FDA-cleared, cloud-based dental AI platform that combines radiographic diagnostic AI (Vision AI, IRIS imaging, CBCT Assist), ambient clinical voice documentation (Overjet Voice), insurance eligibility and claims review automation (Insurance Verification, ReviewPASS), multi-location DSO analytics, and insurer-side Provider Network Management. It is sold primarily as multi-year enterprise subscriptions to DSOs, group dental practices, and dental insurance carriers, with a self-serve entry tier for individual practitioners.
product_offering.product_overview: Overjet offers a unified dental AI platform with a modular architecture that serves dentists, dental service organizations (DSOs), dental insurers, and dental educators. The platform centers on Vision AI (the FDA-cleared diagnostic imaging AI for radiographic analysis that evolved from the original Dental Assist product), IRIS AI-Native Imaging (AI-native dental imaging software, with a separate DSO edition that adds the LENS multi-location layer), and Overjet Voice (the ambient AI documentation suite). These clinical-intelligence products feed Insurance Verification and ReviewPASS (revenue-cycle automation with connections to 300+ payers) and DSO Analytics (the multi-location clinical intelligence dashboard), while CBCT Assist extends the imaging capability to 3D cone beam computed tomography. The Dental Clarity Network (DCN) orchestrates insurer-provider collaboration anchored by ReviewPASS, Provider Network Management handles insurer-side recruiting/data/portal workflows, and the acquired American Dental Examiners (ADE) business provides licensed dental claims review. Together, these products automate clinical decision support, imaging, documentation, and insurance workflows across the dental ecosystem.

product_and_service.description: FDA-cleared vision AI that analyzes dental radiographs to detect and outline dental disease (caries, calculus, periapical radiolucencies, bone loss) and anatomical structures, producing colorized visualizations for diagnosis and patient education; sold to dentists, DSOs, and dental educators (with a separate Educators curriculum edition).
product_and_service.name: Vision AI

product_and_service.description: AI-native dental imaging software that captures crystal-clear images from any sensor, auto-populates templates, and applies FDA-cleared AI analysis in a single integrated workflow, with a separate IRIS DSO edition including the LENS multi-location imaging data layer.
product_and_service.name: IRIS AI-Native Imaging

product_and_service.description: Ambient AI clinical documentation suite that listens to patient visits, generates chart notes, perio charts, and referral letters, monitors calls, and produces automated referrals and structured data for revenue cycle; sold to dental practices and DSOs.
product_and_service.name: Overjet Voice (Voice AI Suite)

product_and_service.description: AI-powered dental insurance eligibility and benefits verification that automatically confirms coverage days in advance with code-level breakdowns, integrating with 300+ payers and syncing to the practice management system (PMS); sold to dental practices and DSOs.

product_and_service.description: Real-time signal covering 300+ procedures that indicates whether a claim will bypass manual clinical review at participating payers, enabling instant approvals; flagship product of the Dental Clarity Network and sold to dental practices, DSOs, and insurers.
product_and_service.name: ReviewPASS

product_and_service.description: Centralized clinical intelligence dashboard that surfaces case acceptance, treatment planning rates, and missed care opportunities across multi-location DSOs (20–200+ locations), allowing drill-down from enterprise KPIs to individual provider radiographic decisions.
product_and_service.name: DSO Analytics

product_and_service.description: FDA 510(k)-cleared AI product for 3D cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) imaging that automatically identifies, labels, segments, and quantifies anatomical structures, providing measurements for periodontal bone levels, airway assessment, implant site evaluation, and surgical planning.

product_and_service.description: Insurer-side suite comprising three modules — Recruiting (nationwide provider data with utilization management insights), Provider Data Management (streamlined provider data and communication hub), and Provider Portal (seamless submissions and updates in one portal) — sold to dental insurance carriers.

recent_move.description: Expanded the Dental Care Alliance partnership so that DCA became the first DSO to deploy Overjet AI (Voice, IRIS, AI Revenue Cycle Management, and Vision) across all 400+ affiliated practices in 24 states, covering the entire patient journey.

Raised a $53.2 million Series C led by March Capital, with participation from the American Dental Association, Crosslink Capital, General Catalyst, Insight Partners, Harmonic Growth Partners, Liquid 2 Ventures, SpringRock Ventures, and E14 Fund.
Launched the Dental Clarity Network (DCN) anchored by the ReviewPASS real-time claims-bypass signal, with major dental providers and insurers including MetLife and Humana joining the initiative.

Received FDA 510(k) clearance for CBCT Assist, an AI product for 3D cone beam computed tomography imaging, marking Overjet's 10th FDA clearance and extending the platform from 2D radiographs into 3D surgical and implant planning.
Acquired DentalBee for an undisclosed amount, expanding the platform's footprint beyond imaging and documentation into adjacent dental software workflows.
Partnered with Spear Education to integrate Overjet's AI-assisted diagnostic tools into dental school curricula and continuing education, opening the dental educator customer segment.

expansion_highlight.description: The June 2026 expansion of the Dental Care Alliance agreement into a full-suite, enterprise-wide deployment covering Voice, IRIS, AI Revenue Cycle Management, and Vision across 400+ practices signals a meaningful land-and-expand motion that converts single-product pilots into platform-wide recurring revenue.

The January 2026 partnership with Spear Education to embed AI diagnostic tools in dental school curricula and continuing education opens the dental educator and future-practitioner segment, creating a top-of-funnel training channel and a long-cycle brand-loyalty moat.

The December 2025 acquisition of DentalBee, combined with the December 2025 $25.4M funding round, indicates both balance-sheet capacity and strategic intent to extend the platform beyond imaging, documentation, and revenue cycle into adjacent dental software categories.

The December 2025 raise (~$25.4M, following the $53.2M Series C in March 2024) shows sustained investor appetite despite a tighter 2024-2025 venture environment, signaling capital for further product expansion and likely sales build-out.

The 10th FDA 510(k) clearance for CBCT Assist in December 2025 expanded the imaging franchise from 2D dental radiographs into 3D cone beam computed tomography, unlocking use cases in implantology, periodontics, airway analysis, and surgical planning and widening the addressable clinical surface area.

Integration partnerships with Medit (AuraVue, incorporating Overjet AI in cloud-based 3D intraoral scanning) and Planet DDS (DentalOS, embedding Overjet alongside Pearl and VideaHealth) extend distribution into third-party imaging and DSO platforms, suggesting channel-led geographic and customer reach expansion without proportional sales headcount.

company_assessment.market_position: Overjet is a venture-backed, Boston-based dental AI company founded in 2018 that positions itself as a leader in clinical decision support and insurance workflow automation for the dental ecosystem. The company serves dentists, Dental Service Organizations (DSOs), dental insurers/payers, and dental schools through a multi-product SaaS platform anchored by 10 FDA clearances, the Dental Care Alliance enterprise rollout across 400+ practices in 24 states, and named customers such as MetLife and Humana on the payer side.

strengths.details: The Dental Clarity Network launched March 2025 with MetLife and Humana as flagship participants, anchored by ReviewPASS — a real-time signal that tells practices whether a claim will bypass manual clinical review. If Overjet successfully recruits additional top-10 dental insurers (the company already counts 16+ major carriers per Series B disclosure), ReviewPASS becomes a two-sided utility that no single competitor can replicate, and per-claim transaction economics could expand margins well beyond traditional SaaS. This is the clearest path to a venture-scale outcome.
strengths.headline: Dental Clarity Network creates winner-take-all utility

strengths.details: Overjet Voice claims ~5+ hours saved per provider per week and a ~25% reduction in claim denials. With ~200,000 practicing dentists in the US and ambient documentation rapidly becoming a baseline expectation (mirroring what Abridge and Nuance DAX have done in medicine), expansion from imaging AI into voice/documentation could 3-5x revenue per existing DSO customer and unlock an entirely new solo-practice and small-group segment via the "Try for free" PLG motion currently in market.
strengths.headline: Voice AI unlocks massive per-dentist TAM expansion

strengths.details: The Dental Care Alliance relationship began in 2022 and has expanded through three documented phases (initial partnership → 2024 full imaging rollout → June 2026 full patient-journey deployment). With ~5,000+ DSOs in the US operating 30%+ of dental practices, even modest penetration of the top 100 DSOs replicates DCA at scale. The acquired American Dental Examiners (June 2021) and DentalBee (December 2025) also signal an M&A roll-up strategy to consolidate claims-review and adjacent workflows.
strengths.headline: Land-and-expand model replicates across thousands of DSOs

strengths.details: CBCT Assist received FDA 510(k) clearance in December 2025 — Overjet's 10th FDA clearance — extending AI from 2D to 3D imaging for implant, surgical, and airway planning. With 3D CBCT scanners becoming standard in mid-market practices and implants representing a high-value revenue line (~$5K-$50K per case), AI-guided implant case capture via the Implant Finder feature alone could unlock a multi-hundred-million-dollar revenue category distinct from the existing subscription base.
strengths.headline: CBCT Assist and Implant Finder expand into high-value surgical revenue

strengths.details: Overjet counts 10 FDA clearances, HITRUST CSF certification, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA compliance — a regulatory and security posture that few dental AI competitors can match and that effectively blocks new entrants from selling into enterprise DSOs and insurers. Combined with integrations into Medit AuraVue and Planet DDS DentalOS, Overjet is positioned as the default AI layer across the dental software stack, justifying premium pricing and pricing power as the category matures.
strengths.headline: 10 FDA clearances create durable regulatory moat

weakness.details: Planet DDS's DentalOS platform lists Overjet alongside direct competitors Pearl and VideaHealth as interchangeable AI imaging vendors, signaling a commoditization risk where DSO customers can swap vendors with limited switching cost. If a competitor undercuts pricing or achieves comparable FDA-cleared accuracy, Overjet's $425M+ valuation could compress materially. The dental AI category is attracting significant capital from strategic acquirers (Henry Schein acquired VideaHealth in 2024), which may accelerate consolidation and pressure standalone players.
weakness.headline: Pearl and VideaHealth commoditize dental imaging AI

weakness.details: Overjet's marquee customer Dental Care Alliance accounts for 400+ practices across 24 states, and the June 2026 expansion makes DCA Overjet's flagship reference account. Any churn, budget cut, or strategic change at DCA would have an outsized impact on revenue, given the limited number of disclosed enterprise DSO logos (CoreDental, Jefferson Dental, The Smilist, Dental 365, North American Dental, Platinum Dental). Concentration in a handful of large DSOs leaves the revenue base vulnerable to a single relationship deteriorating.
weakness.headline: DCA customer concentration creates revenue fragility

weakness.details: Overjet's last disclosed post-money valuation was $425M in December 2021. With ~$80M raised since then across Series C ($53.2M in March 2024 led by March Capital) and a $25.36M extension in December 2025, the company has either marked up meaningfully in private rounds or faces flat/down rounds in a tighter 2024-2025 AI funding environment. The lack of disclosed current valuation is a material gap, and any IPO path is likely several years away given AI market conditions.
weakness.headline: Last valuation disclosure is 4+ years stale

weakness.details: While FDA clearance is a current moat, increasing FTC and HHS scrutiny of AI in clinical decision support, plus ongoing debates around algorithmic bias in healthcare AI, could impose new validation, monitoring, or disclosure requirements. The CBCT Assist clearance and 10 total clearances create regulatory surface area that must be maintained; any adverse event or recall could compromise market positioning and trigger costly remediation across the entire platform.
weakness.headline: Regulatory scrutiny of clinical AI is tightening

weakness.details: Overjet has expanded from a single Vision AI product in 2021 to a portfolio spanning imaging AI, ambient voice documentation, insurance verification, RCM analytics, and payer provider-network tools — five distinct product categories with different buyers, competitors, and integration requirements. Ambient documentation alone competes against well-funded players like Abridge, Suki, and Nuance DAX in healthcare AI. Execution risk across this portfolio may strain engineering and sales resources, slowing the path to profitability.
weakness.headline: Product sprawl dilutes execution focus

competitive_moat.details: Overjet holds 10 FDA 510(k) clearances across its imaging AI products, including the first FDA clearance ever granted to a dental AI company (Dental Assist, August 2021) and the more recent CBCT Assist clearance for 3D imaging. Each clearance represents a multi-year, data-intensive regulatory investment that is difficult and expensive for competitors to replicate in a clinical decision-support category.

Enterprise-scale deployments across DSOs such as Dental Care Alliance (400+ practices in 24 states), TD Dental (34 locations), and integrations with 300+ insurance payers generate a continuous, clinically labeled data flywheel that improves model accuracy on caries detection, bone loss measurement, and clinical review automation. Volume and diversity of data is structurally hard for later entrants to match.

Platform integrations with practice management systems, sensors (IRIS), 300+ payer connections, and embedded clinical workflows (chart notes, perio charts, automated referrals, revenue cycle) create high operational switching costs once a DSO or payer is deployed. Customers report 18x ROI and 25%+ case acceptance lifts that anchor multi-year contracts.

Overjet has built a defensible go-to-market by winning flagship DSO accounts (Dental Care Alliance, Core Dental, Jefferson Dental, Aligned Dental Partners, The Smilist, Dental 365, North American Dental Group, Platinum Dental Services) and major insurers (MetLife, Humana, plus 16 carriers by December 2021). Land-and-expand is reinforced by integration partnerships with Medit (AuraVue) and Planet DDS (DentalOS), extending distribution without adding direct sales headcount.

The Dental Clarity Network (DCN) and ReviewPASS create a two-sided payer-provider network effect: more payer participation increases ReviewPASS signal coverage (300+ procedures), which in turn increases the platform's value to dental practices. This network, combined with the Spear Education curriculum partnership, is converting the product from point solution into industry infrastructure.

Overjet was the first dental AI company to receive FDA clearance, has 10 cumulative clearances, and is consistently positioned as the category leader by customers and investors, supported by HITRUST, HIPAA, SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, and CCPA certifications. These compliance and brand assets lower enterprise procurement risk.

key_risks.details: Dental Care Alliance's 400+ practices across 24 states represent Overjet's most prominent reference account and the anchor of its land-and-expand DSO strategy. With only a handful of other DSO logos disclosed (CoreDental, Jefferson Dental, The Smilist, Dental 365, North American Dental, Platinum Dental), churn or budget compression at any single large DSO would have outsized impact on revenue concentration risk.
key_risks.headline: DCA customer concentration creates revenue fragility

key_risks.details: Planet DDS's DentalOS platform lists Overjet, Pearl, and VideaHealth as interchangeable AI imaging vendors, signaling commoditization risk and limited switching costs at the DSO buyer level. Henry Schein's 2024 acquisition of VideaHealth and well-funded entrants like Pearl continue to compress pricing power and could trigger a feature/price race that pressures margins.
key_risks.headline: Dental imaging AI faces accelerating competitive pressure

key_risks.details: Overjet has raised approximately $155M+ across seed ($7.85M), Series A ($27M), Series B ($42.5M), Series C ($53.2M, March 2024), and a December 2025 extension ($25.36M). The pace of funding and headcount of 101-250 employees suggest a continued reliance on external capital to fund sales, RCM, payer-side, and Voice product expansion before reaching self-sustaining cash flow.
key_risks.headline: Capital intensity remains elevated with ~$155M+ raised

key_risks.details: The Series B post-money valuation of $425M was disclosed in December 2021. No pre/post-money valuations are disclosed for the 2024 Series C or the 2025 extension, leaving current mark-to-market unclear and creating uncertainty for any secondary transactions or IPO planning in an AI-market-sensitive environment.
key_risks.headline: Last disclosed valuation is 4+ years old

key_risks.details: Overjet Voice enters the ambient clinical documentation market where competitors like Abridge (medicine), Suki, and Nuance DAX have raised billions in capital and are extending into dental. Overjet must compete for talent, integrations, and accuracy benchmarks against companies with substantially larger war chests and broader clinical footprints beyond dentistry.
key_risks.headline: Voice AI is a contested, well-funded category

key_risks.details: With 10 FDA clearances covering diagnostic interpretation across 2D radiographs and 3D CBCT scans, any misdiagnosis, algorithmic failure, or FDA post-market surveillance issue exposes Overjet to clinical liability, recall costs, and reputational damage in a category where accuracy is being actively marketed (Overjet claims >90% accuracy).
key_risks.headline: Regulatory and clinical liability risk is real

key_highlights.details: Overjet is rolling out its full AI suite (Overjet Voice, IRIS AI-Native Imaging, AI Revenue Cycle Management, and Vision) across DCA's 400+ affiliated practices in 24 states — described as one of the most ambitious AI deployments in dentistry. The relationship began in 2022 and expanded through documented phases, demonstrating a clear land-and-expand motion that scales revenue per customer materially.
key_highlights.headline: Landmark DSO deployment at Dental Care Alliance

key_highlights.details: Overjet holds 10 FDA 510(k) clearances across its platform, including the first FDA clearance ever granted to a dental AI company (Dental Assist, August 2021) and the December 2025 CBCT Assist clearance for 3D imaging. FDA-cleared status is a prerequisite for selling into enterprise DSOs and payers, and the cumulative clearance footprint is a meaningful barrier for new entrants.
key_highlights.headline: 10 FDA clearances create regulatory moat

key_highlights.details: Launched March 2025 with MetLife and Humana as flagship participants, the Dental Clarity Network — anchored by ReviewPASS — positions Overjet as a two-sided platform between payers and providers. The Series B disclosure (Dec 2021) noted 16 major insurance carriers as customers, validating payer distribution as a real wedge into revenue-cycle automation.
key_highlights.headline: Payer-side anchor: Dental Clarity Network with MetLife and Humana

key_highlights.details: Overjet is HIPAA-compliant, HITRUST CSF certified, SOC 2 Type II compliant, GDPR-compliant (with UK/EU Standard Contractual Clauses), and CCPA-compliant. This certification stack is required for enterprise DSO and payer contracts and is held by very few dental AI competitors.
key_highlights.headline: Robust enterprise security and compliance posture

key_highlights.details: The platform spans Vision AI (diagnostic imaging), IRIS (AI-native imaging software), Overjet Voice (ambient documentation), Insurance Verification (300+ payer connections), ReviewPASS (instant claim approvals), DSO Analytics, and CBCT Assist — bundling clinical intelligence, imaging, documentation, and revenue cycle into a single enterprise sale. Customers report ~25% reduction in claim denials and ~5+ hours saved per provider per week via Voice.
key_highlights.headline: Multi-product platform diversifies revenue per customer

key_highlights.details: Overjet has raised ~$155M+ across rounds, with backing from General Catalyst, Insight Partners, March Capital (Series C lead, March 2024), Crosslink Capital, and the American Dental Association. The December 2025 $25.36M extension demonstrates continued investor appetite post-Series C despite a tougher 2024-2025 AI funding environment.
key_highlights.headline: Strong investor syndicate and continued funding momentum

key_highlights.details: Overjet acquired American Dental Examiners (ADE) in June 2021 to add licensed dental claims review services to its payer offerings, and acquired DentalBee in December 2025 to bolster capabilities. A roll-up strategy around clinical and revenue-cycle AI positions Overjet to consolidate fragmented dental-services software.
key_highlights.headline: Strategic acquisitions extend platform breadth

customer_concentration.details: Customer concentration is best characterized as Moderate to High. Dental Care Alliance (400+ practices across 24 states) is by far the largest publicly named customer, and the relationship has progressed from a 2022 initial partnership to a June 2026 full-suite enterprise deployment, meaning a material share of Overjet's DSO revenue base is likely tied to a single anchor account. On the payer side, the December 2021 disclosure of 16 major insurance carriers as customers, combined with the March 2025 named commitments from MetLife and Humana to the Dental Clarity Network, diversifies revenue across at least two national carriers but also concentrates platform importance in a small number of large payers. The remaining named DSO logos (TD Dental, Core Dental, Jefferson Dental, Aligned Dental Partners, The Smilist, Dental 365, North American Dental Group, Platinum Dental Services) plus the self-serve "Try for free" funnel suggest a mid- and long-tail base exists, but the absence of disclosed revenue figures prevents a definitive split; loss of DCA or one of the top three payers would meaningfully affect revenue predictability.

peers.description: Pearl is the closest direct competitor to Overjet, offering FDA-cleared AI for dental radiograph analysis and pathology detection. Both companies compete head-to-head for DSO and dental practice contracts, and Pearl is explicitly listed alongside Overjet as an interchangeable AI imaging vendor on Planet DDS's DentalOS platform.
peers.name: Pearl (Pearl AI)

peers.description: VideaHealth is a dental AI imaging competitor that was acquired by Henry Schein in 2024, giving it distribution advantage through the largest dental distributor. It directly competes with Overjet's Vision AI for the same DSO and group practice customers, and is similarly positioned as a Planet DDS DentalOS integration partner.
peers.name: VideaHealth (Henry Schein)

peers.description: Denti.AI is an earlier-stage dental AI company offering image analysis for dental radiographs, voice charting, and insurance verification — overlapping with both Vision AI and Overjet Voice. It represents a smaller, more focused competitor in the same dental AI category.
peers.name: Denti.AI

peers.description: Planet DDS provides Denticon, an AI-native DSO enterprise platform, and has integrated Overjet alongside Pearl and VideaHealth as AI imaging options. It is both a channel partner and an adjacent competitor in DSO workflow software, making it a key distribution dependency and a strategic threat if it builds competing AI capabilities.
peers.name: Planet DDS (DentalOS)

peers.description: 3Shape is a global dental technology incumbent offering intraoral scanners, CAD/CAM software, and digital workflow tools. Its Medit AuraVue partner platform integrates Overjet AI, illustrating how traditional dental imaging companies rely on Overjet as a software layer; the relationship is symbiotic but 3Shape is a potential horizontal competitor.
peers.name: 3Shape

peers.description: Align Technology operates the Invisalign system and iTero intraoral scanners — both embedded in dental practices — and has invested in AI-powered imaging and treatment planning. While not a direct competitor today, Align's scanner data and AI investments make it a strategic incumbent that could compete with Overjet's imaging AI in the orthodontic and restorative segments.
peers.name: Align Technology (iTero)

peers.description: Dentsply Sirona is one of the largest global dental equipment and digital solutions companies, offering imaging systems (including CBCT), practice management software, and a growing AI/digital workflow portfolio. It is a broad incumbent in the same dental practices Overjet targets and has the resources to bundle AI capabilities into its hardware stack.
peers.name: Dentsply Sirona

peers.description: Henry Schein One is the technology and practice management arm of Henry Schein, offering Dentrix and other dental software to a large installed base. Following Henry Schein's acquisition of VideaHealth, it directly distributes a competing dental AI platform, making it both a broad incumbent and an indirect competitor to Overjet in the DSO and group practice segment.
peers.name: Henry Schein One

peers.description: Curve Dental provides cloud-based practice management software for dental practices and DSOs, and has begun integrating AI capabilities into its platform. It represents an emerging cloud-native competitor and potential distribution channel for AI features that could compete with or complement Overjet's clinical intelligence products.
peers.name: Curve Dental

peers.description: tab32 is a cloud-based dental practice management and imaging platform with growing AI capabilities, serving DSOs and dental practices. As an emerging cloud-native player with AI ambitions, it competes in adjacent workflow software and could expand into diagnostic AI to compete with Overjet.
peers.name: tab32
